question.text: Under Schedule B, Clause 4(3) of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015, trading window restrictions do NOT apply to which of the following?

answer.text: Purchase of shares from the open market by designated persons
Subscribing to rights issue, tendering shares in a buy-back offer, or open offer
Sale of shares by promoters through stock exchange
Open market purchase of shares by key managerial personnel

explanation.text: The Logic: Schedule B, Clause 4(3)(b) of the SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 lists categories of transactions that are exempt from trading window restrictions — acquisition by conversion of warrants/debentures, subscribing to a rights issue, further public issue, preferential allotment, and tendering shares in a buy-back/open offer/delisting offer (NISM Series III-A workbook p. 127). Option B aligns with this list and is uniquely correct. The Trap: Option A (open market purchase by designated persons) and option C (sale of shares by promoters through stock exchange) are discretionary market trades, which are squarely subject to the trading window. Option D — originally written as "preferential basis" — was ambiguous because Schedule B Clause 4(3)(b) actually exempts preferential allotment, which would have made option D also defensible. Option D has been rewritten as "Open market purchase of shares by key managerial personnel", which is clearly non-exempt. Note: The audit flagged the original option D ("preferential basis") because that wording overlapped with one of the Schedule B exemptions, allowing two options to be correct. Option D has been rewritten to be unambiguously non-exempt, keeping B as the uniquely correct keyed answer (Source: NISM Series III-A Securities Intermediaries Compliance workbook, p. 127).
